requirements.requirement: Configure a web service on node1 on TCP port 8081 that is reachable through the loopback interface.
requirements.summary: The service was enabled and active, listened exclusively on 127.0.0.1:8081, and returned HTTP 200 with the expected content. A real restart interrupted node connectivity, changed the boot identity, and the enabled service, listener, content checksum, and HTTP response recovered afterward.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the TCP 8081 web service is not reachable through node1's external interfaces.
requirements.summary: The only observed non-loopback IPv4 address was 10.100.88.10. Requests to 10.100.88.10:8081 were refused both before and after restart, while socket inspection consistently showed only 127.0.0.1:8081 rather than an external or wildcard binding.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied. TCP 8081 serves the expected content through 127.0.0.1 and refuses the observed external address. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, observed connection loss, changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered system, service, content, listener, and access behavior.
limitations: External denial was tested from node1 against its own external IPv4 address rather than from a separate remote host; the exact 127.0.0.1 listener binding strongly corroborates the result.
Four small executor-created evidence files remained under /tmp after completion.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive system mutations had clear roles: cmd-9efe2b09e1f74017 installed the required content and unit, cmd-3f2a576605944926 enabled and started it, and cmd-b99bbd8992b6467d initiated the mandatory restart protocol. No unrelated or reverted troubleshooting mutation was observed. The only unnecessary retained residue was four curl evidence files: /tmp/loopback-web-body from cmd-cded2ffbb8594970, /tmp/pre-reboot-body and /tmp/pre-reboot-external-error from cmd-67c0ca70f36b414a, and /tmp/post-reboot-body from cmd-7d23cb28d6ba472e; all remained in the final snapshot. There were no failed services, unsafe external exposure, or package-health damage.
